Thought: To solve this problem, I need to determine which pairs correctly represent an acid and its conjugate base. The conjugate base of an acid is formed by the loss of a proton (H⁺) from the acid. I will evaluate each pair to determine this relationship.

- Option A: H2NCH2CO2H (acid) and H2NCH2CO2^- (conjugate base) - This pair correctly shows an acid losing a proton from the carboxyl group to form its conjugate base.
- Option B: H2NCH2CO2H (acid) and H3N^+CH2CO2^- - This pair does not represent an acid and its conjugate base, as the loss of a proton from the acid does not result in the given conjugate.
- Option C: H3N^+CH2CO2H (acid) and H3N^+CH2CO2^- (conjugate base) - This pair correctly shows the acid losing a proton from the carboxyl group.
- Option D: H3N^+CH2CO2^- (acid) and H2NCH2CO2^- (conjugate base) - This pair correctly represents the acid losing a proton from the ammonium group.

The pair that does not correctly show an acid and its conjugate base is option B.
